ChatGPT said:

Yes. Your list is a strong starting point for NephroReach's community chat. However, because your members include dialysis and advanced CKD patients, I would add several safeguards beyond simply detecting words.

The most important addition is a tiered moderation system that distinguishes potential medical emergencies, patient safety concerns, and inappropriate community behavior.

1. Additional auto-flag words

Priority 1

Potential medical emergencies

Add these phrases to your existing emergency list:

  • "Chest pressure"

  • "Can't wake up"

  • "Not breathing"

  • "Trouble speaking"

  • "Face drooping"

  • "One-sided weakness"

  • "Severe allergic reaction"

  • "Throat closing"

  • "Coughing up blood"

  • "Vomiting blood"

  • "Bleeding won't stop"

  • "Missed multiple treatments"

  • "Potassium is high"

Priority 2

Dialysis-specific concerns

  • "Catheter fell out"

  • "Catheter came out"

  • "Catheter pulled out"

  • "Fistula stopped working"

  • "No buzzing"

  • "No vibration"

  • "Access clotted"

  • "Access not working"

  • "Missed dialysis"

  • "Can't get dialysis"

  • "Can't get a treatment"

  • "Machine alarm"

  • "Cloudy PD fluid"

  • "Cloudy drain bag"

  • "Severe abdominal pain"

  • "Can't drain"

  • "Can't fill"

  • "Exit site infection"

Priority 2

Mental health and personal safety

  • "I don't want to live"

  • "Better off dead"

  • "End my life"

  • "Overdose"

  • "Someone is hurting me"

  • "I'm being threatened"

  • "I don't feel safe"

  • "I can't take this anymore"

Priority 3

Privacy, scams and unsafe advice

  • "Social Security number"

  • "Bank account"

  • "Credit card number"

  • "Send me your password"

  • "Send your medical records"

  • "DM me your information"

  • "Stop taking your medication"

  • "You don't need dialysis"

  • "Double your dose"

  • "Miracle cure"

  • "Guaranteed cure"

  • "Send me money"

These are screening terms, not diagnoses. For example, "high potassium" alone does not establish an emergency, and "I went to the ER yesterday" is not necessarily a current crisis.

2. Give your developer three different alert levels

Level 1 — Potential emergency

Urgent

Examples: chest pain, difficulty breathing, uncontrolled access bleeding, suicidal intent.

System response:

  • Immediately display an emergency safety message.

  • Flag the message for priority moderator review.

  • Provide a prominent 911 option for immediate danger.

  • Do not wait for a moderator before showing emergency instructions.

Level 2 — Medical or safety concern

Review

Examples: missed dialysis, medication questions, access concerns, possible infection.

System response:

  • Display a message directing the member to their care team.

  • Add the post to the moderation queue.

  • Prevent other members from giving individualized medical instructions through community moderation rules.

Level 3 — Community violations

Moderation

Examples: harassment, scams, threats, sharing another person's private information.

System response:

  • Hold high-risk posts for review when appropriate.

  • Allow moderators to warn, remove, or restrict users.

  • Record moderation decisions and appeals.

3. Improve your automatic replies

I would not use the same reply for every flagged word. Your current response is appropriate for general medical concerns, but someone reporting active chest pain needs more direct guidance.

Developer-ready automatic replies

Automatic message preview

Your message may describe a medical emergency. If you are experiencing chest pain, severe difficulty breathing, uncontrolled bleeding, or other immediate danger, call 911 now. NephroReach is not an emergency response service. Your message is not automatically sent to emergency services or your dialysis team.

4. Additional developer requirements

These are especially important for NephroReach's multi-tenant structure and patient privacy.

Development checklist

0/6

One important policy decision: A flagged message should not automatically be transmitted to a dialysis facility or nephrologist. That would require a separate, clearly defined communication workflow, appropriate permissions, and confirmation that the receiving team has agreed to monitor that channel.

Before launch, have your healthcare attorney and clinical safety reviewer examine the moderation policy, emergency disclaimers, privacy practices, and escalation procedures. This will help ensure the system's promises match what NephroReach can actually deliver.
